data.hypothesis: The final warp reduction combines only four warp partials, but the generic 32-lane tree performs five shuffle stages. Using only offsets 2 and 1 preserves the same integer reduction order for lane 0 while reducing that stage to two shuffles. This may reduce per-block instruction cost without changing synchronization, mapping, or recursive passes; the whole-call effect remains unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: This recursive reduction variant and its 128-thread mapping; the result does not establish which kernel change caused the difference.
memory_lessons.claim: The selected parent passed all 10 reported cases and measured 30.8038 microseconds over three samples, versus the baseline's 46.4832 microseconds over three samples. This is a whole-call result, not a measurement of the block reduction alone.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the four-partial two-shuffle variant with the same correctness cases and repeated full-call protocol.

data.notes: The parent is valid on the reported cases and its repeated full-call mean was lower than the baseline's; that does not prove the block-reduction mechanism caused the difference. This proposal has not been compiled, validated, or measured. The controller should check all required inputs, seeds, bounds, guards, and repeated full-call timings before drawing conclusions.
transformations: Replace the final warp's generic five-stage reduction of four 64-bit warp partials with explicit shuffle-down stages at offsets 2 and 1.

Keep the 128-thread, one-element-per-lane mapping, 64-bit intermediate accumulation, shared partial exchange and barrier, recursive global passes, scratch layout, launch stream behavior, and final copy unchanged.
